item.text:
Refactored the construction and spawning path so actors are no longer used as simulator prototypes. [Simulator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R011_module_java/Simulator.java:15) now uses explicit `ActorCreationRule` entries with factories and habitat flags instead of a `Map<Actor, Double>`, which removes the old “construct actors just to ask what they are” pattern and makes population order deterministic.

I also separated construction from field registration. [Actor.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R011_module_java/Actor.java:38) now stores its initial location without immediately placing itself, and [Animal.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R011_module_java/Animal.java:256) / [Plant.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R011_module_java/Plant.java:138) register offspring only after they are fully created. [Field.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R011_module_java/Field.java:325) also has a habitat-check overload for raw land/water capabilities, so simulator spawning no longer depends on temporary actor instances.

On the UI side, [SimulatorView.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R011_module_java/SimulatorView.java:61) now builds and shows the frame via `display()` instead of doing Swing container work in the constructor. That cleaned up the last constructor-time escape warning.

Verification: `javac -Xlint:all *.java` now passes with no warnings. I did not run the Swing simulation UI.
